---
title: "Week 10 — Map Visualization — Module II"
---

> Maps people can touch. The second map module moves from static thematic maps to interactive, web-ready maps and embeds them in a Streamlit geospatial dashboard.

## 📖 Background & Motivation

Static maps answer a fixed question; interactive maps let users ask their own. For geographic data — where users almost always want to zoom to *their* region, hover for exact values, or toggle layers — interactivity is often what makes a map useful rather than merely decorative. This module builds on the cartographic foundations from Module I and adds the web layer: tile-based interactive maps with `folium` (Leaflet) and `plotly`, and the patterns for embedding them in a Streamlit app.

The deeper goal is the geospatial *dashboard*: a coordinated view where a map, a filter, and a chart update together. This is the first time the course combines a modality with full interactivity in an app, and it is direct preparation for the final project, where a Streamlit client will display model output that may itself be geographic. We also confront performance — interactive maps with many features can choke a browser — and the design discipline of not drowning the user in layers and popups.

---

## 🔎 Learning Objectives

- Build interactive tile-based maps with folium and plotly.
- Embed and coordinate maps inside a Streamlit dashboard.
- Add interactivity (hover, popups, layer toggles, region filters) without overwhelming the user.
- Manage performance and legibility for many-feature interactive maps.

## 🧭 Two-Hour Session Outline

> Single 2-hour block. Tooling/interactive week — hands-on dominates.

### Block 1 — Concepts & Theory (~20 min, PowerPoint)

1. Static vs. interactive: when interactivity earns its cost (6 min)
2. Tile maps and the web map model (folium/Leaflet, plotly) (8 min)
3. Coordinated dashboards: map + filter + chart updating together (6 min)

### Block 2 — Guided Demonstration (~35 min, live coding)

1. Build an interactive choropleth in folium with hover/popups (12 min)
2. Embed it in Streamlit with `streamlit-folium` (10 min)
3. Add a region filter that updates both the map and a side chart (13 min)

### ☕ Break (~10 min)

### Block 3 — Hands-On Activity (~45 min, students working)

1. Students build an interactive map of their Module I data (15 min)
2. Embed it in a Streamlit dashboard with at least one filter (20 min)
3. Add a coordinated chart that responds to the same filter (10 min)

### Block 4 — Wrap-Up & Homework Preview (~10 min)

1. Demo a few dashboards; discuss performance/legibility trade-offs (6 min)
2. Preview homework — and note this is the pattern the final project builds on (4 min)

## 💻 Notebook / App Snippets

### Interactive folium choropleth

```python
import folium
m = folium.Map(location=[39.0, -98.0], zoom_start=4)
folium.Choropleth(
    geo_data=geojson, data=df,
    columns=["region_id", "rate"], key_on="feature.properties.region_id",
    fill_color="OrRd", legend_name="Rate per 100k",
).add_to(m)
```

### Embed in Streamlit with a filter

```python
# app.py
import streamlit as st
from streamlit_folium import st_folium
import folium

st.title("Geospatial Dashboard")
metric = st.sidebar.selectbox("Metric", ["rate", "count"])

m = folium.Map(location=[39.0, -98.0], zoom_start=4)
folium.Choropleth(
    geo_data=geojson, data=df,
    columns=["region_id", metric], key_on="feature.properties.region_id",
    fill_color="OrRd",
).add_to(m)
st_folium(m, width=700, height=450)
```

### Coordinated side chart

```python
import streamlit as st
top = df.sort_values(metric, ascending=False).head(10)
st.bar_chart(top.set_index("region_name")[metric])
```

2. Include: an interactive map, at least one filter, and one coordinated chart that responds to it.
3. Write a short note on a performance or legibility decision you made.
4. Deploy it and submit the live URL plus repo link to Blackboard.
